$comment: THE AGENTIC CORPUS — the population the product sentence is actually about.
Keel's published corpus is fifteen repositories, pooled 0.853, and thirteen of the fourteen
measured are human-maintained open source. The banner over that number reads 'your agents are
grading their own homework'. The one agent-built target in it — Keel itself — scored 0.357, by
far the lowest, and was described as the corpus floor when it was really the only on-thesis
data point. This corpus is the missing population.
THE SELECTION PREDICATE, committed before any target here was measured so that it cannot be
revised after seeing a score:
A target qualifies if MORE THAN 50% of its last 200 commits carry an agent trailer.
Agent trailers, case-insensitive, matched against the commit body:
Co-Authored-By: Claude | Devin | Codex | Cursor | aider
'Generated with [Claude Code]' / 'Generated with Codex' / 'Generated with Cursor'
'🤖 Generated with'
Excluded: any trailer whose DISPLAY NAME contains '[bot]' or '-bot@' — dependabot and renovate
are automation, not agent authorship. The exclusion is on the display name rather than the whole
line on purpose: Devin's genuine trailer is 'Devin AI <devin-ai-integration[bot]@...>', and a
whole-line rule would erase the very agent the predicate names.
The predicate is mechanically checkable from git log alone, which is what makes the selection
criterion itself anchored: no judgment of ours decides who is in this corpus.
THE BIAS THIS PREDICATE HAS, stated here rather than discovered later.
It measures SURVIVING TRAILERS, not agent authorship. A squash merge drops the commit body, so
agent-heavy projects that merge through a queue score near zero: openai/codex and sst/opencode
both measured 0.000 across their last 200 commits. Every repository that clears 50% is therefore
one where agent commits land on the default branch with their bodies intact — typically
solo-maintainer or small-org repos. This corpus is biased toward small teams and away from large
organisations with merge hygiene, and any ratio computed over it inherits that bias. 93
repositories were cloned and counted to assemble these six.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and why it matters more than what was included:
- Agent TOOLING. Repositories that exist to serve coding agents (claudekit, catacomb,
claude-code-templates, amplifier, agent-of-empires, ...) all qualified, several at higher
rates than the targets chosen. They are excluded because a finding drawn from them is
attackable as 'repos built for agents have unusual CI' rather than a fact about
agent-written code. Every target below is an ordinary product: a karaoke pipeline, a
zero-knowledge proof system, a data engine, a build CLI, a query language, an agent-memory
server.
- broomva/* — 26 of 30 clear the predicate, and they share an author with Keel. Measuring
them would be measuring ourselves twice.
- Copyleft licences, because this corpus quotes CI snippets as evidence in a published report.
VENDOR CONCENTRATION, disclosed. Five of six are Claude-trailered; kody is Cursor. Across 93
repositories scanned, kody was the only non-Claude agent-authored repository found at scale, and
that scarcity is itself a finding about what is publicly observable today. A corpus that were
100% one vendor would be attackable as an artifact of one tool's conventions, so kody is here
specifically to weaken that objection — not to remove it.
ACCEPTANCE. The run answers one stated question: how many of these score exactly 1.000, and does
the pooled agentic ratio differ from the published human-maintained 0.853 by more than 0.10?
Both answers are reportable results. If agent-maintained repositories score just as well, that
is a finding against the product's own thesis and it gets published in the same voice.
Node cap 25, matching the published corpus so the two are comparable. The cap is disclosed
beside every ratio, and the summary derives it from the recorded entries rather than from this
declaration.

targets.name: karaoke-gen
targets.culture: Python karaoke-video pipeline — stem separation, lyric sync, CDG render, upload. MIT. 196/200 = 0.980 Claude-trailered. 7 workflows incl. e2e-daily and a DR backup-freshness check, plus a Makefile.

targets.name: kody
targets.culture: TypeScript portable agent-memory server on Cloudflare Workers. FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available, converts to Apache-2.0). 192/200 = 0.960 CURSOR-trailered — the vendor-diversity target. CI: validate, deploy, preview, dr-escrow.

targets.name: binius64
targets.culture: Rust binary-field zero-knowledge proof system. MIT + Apache-2.0. 178/200 = 0.890. CI: ci.yml, docs.yml. Cryptography — a domain where a wrong test is expensive and the maintainers know it.

targets.name: xorq
targets.culture: Python executable-memory engine for tabular data, Ibis-derived. Apache-2.0. 169/200 = 0.845. 24 workflows including a CI matrix across BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, S3 and GCS — the heaviest integration surface in this corpus.

targets.name: aspect-cli
targets.culture: Rust + Starlark Bazel-compatible build CLI. Apache-2.0. 140/200 = 0.700. Deliberately included for its CI shape: Buildkite AND CircleCI AND GitLab CI AND 12 GitHub workflows AND MODULE.bazel. Keel reads two of those five, so this target exercises the unread-surfaces disclosure rather than only the ratio.

targets.name: wvlet
targets.culture: Scala flow-style query language compiling to SQL engines. Apache-2.0. 129/200 = 0.645. 17 workflows spanning JVM, Python and TypeScript test lanes — the only JVM-ecosystem target in either corpus.
